Alloy-level (not specific to this 575 °C / 3 h sample): the 15Al alloy density measured by Archimedes method = 6.85 g·cm−3, and its EDS composition is Fe 44.6, Mn 35.2, Al 15.0, Cu 5.2 (at.%).
Alloy-level: elastic modulus E = 164 GPa for 15Al (measured through compressive stress–strain curves), used in the indentation fracture-toughness Eq. (1).

The properties reported for the 15Al alloy's hardest condition (600 °C / 6 h) — peak Vickers hardness 965.6 HV, specific hardness 141 HV·cm3/g, nanoindentation average hardness 11.7 ± 0.4 GPa, β-Mn intrinsic hardness 12.1 ± 0.3 GPa, average crack length 18 µm and KIC = 8.6 MPa·m1/2 — belong to that peak-hardness sample, not to this 575 °C / 3 h sample.
In Table 2, the 15Al 575 °C aging series is: 1 h = 752.6 ± 50.7 HV, 3 h = 935.5 ± 15.8 HV, 6 h = 960.3 ± 6.8 HV, 10 h = 957.8 ± 10.1 HV; the 3 h hardness lies just below the 6 h peak.

The SE-SEM images of the 15Al 575 °C / 1 h condition show 'Untransformed α' with needle-like precipitates (α-Mn and β-Mn labels), whereas by 575 °C / 3 h the matrix appears essentially featureless/uniform (figure_007).

β-Mn in the hardest Fe-Mn-Al-Cu samples is Mn-rich (~36.8 at.% Mn) and poor in Al and Cu (~14.3 at.% Al, ~2.8 at.% Cu for the 15Al alloy) according to SEM-EDS (figure_014); this composition data pertains to the 15Al hardest sample, not specifically the 575 °C / 3 h sample.
